## What was built

Implementation files (root package, one responsibility each):
- `integer.mbt` — `HpackReader` forward cursor and section 5.1 prefixed integers. Values are accumulated in `Int64` so the `2^31−1` limit is exact; >5 continuation octets or a larger value is `IntegerOverflow`, a truncated integer is `UnexpectedEof`. `write_int` emits minimal encodings.
- `huffman_table.mbt` — the Appendix B 257-symbol code/bit-length tables, extracted programmatically from `specs/rfc7541.txt` (verified 257/257 complete).
- `huffman.mbt` — a flat decode trie built once, plus encode (MSB-first, ones padding) and decode with section 5.2 validation (EOS, >7 bits padding, non-ones padding → `InvalidHuffman`).
- `string_literal.mbt` — raw/Huffman string literals with the H bit and 7-bit length.
- `static_table.mbt` — the 61-entry Appendix A table (tuple entries to avoid record-type ambiguity with `HeaderField`).
- `dynamic_table.mbt` — `HeaderField::size` (`name+value+32`) and the dynamic table: newest-first, exact size accounting, eviction on insert/size-change, oversized-entry rule.
- `decoder.mbt` / `encoder.mbt` — opaque `pub struct`s with private fields, implementing all five representations and the deterministic greedy encoder plus non-indexing forms and section 4.2 size-update signalling (`set_max_size`).

`Decoder`/`Encoder` are opaque (regenerated `.mbti` shows `pub struct … { // private fields }`), matching the `declare pub type` contract.

- Added RFC conformance tests verify Appendix C.2–C.6 **in both directions** — every block is compared byte-for-byte with the RFC hex dump and decoded back to the expected fields, including the 256-octet-table response stories with between-block eviction.
- Added white-box tests cover the whole Huffman alphabet, the Appendix C.1 integer examples, and the overflow boundary; added black-box tests cover each decoding-error condition and the section 4.4 "name survives eviction" rule.
- Independent cross-implementation validation: the codec decoded the entire public `hpack-test-case` corpus — **47,142 cases across 478 stories from go-hpack, nghttp2, python-hpack, node, haskell-http2 and swift-nio, with 0 failures**. ## Behavior implemented
- Line classification: blank / full-line `;`|`#` comment / `[section]` / key-value; a `[` in a value is never a section.
- Sections: trimmed names, one surrounding quote pair stripped, bracket-free + non-empty required; repeated headers re-open and accumulate; empty sections recorded; last-wins keys.
- Entries: first `=` or `:` is the separator; keys trimmed, non-empty, control-char-free, verbatim (not escape-decoded); values trimmed unless quoted.
- Quoted values: closing quote on same line only, followed only by blanks/optional comment; per-carrier escapes (`"..."`: `\\ \n \r \t \"`; `'...'`: only `\\ \'`; unquoted: `\\ \n \r \t`), everything else kept as written.
- Continuation: decided on the raw line by odd/even trailing-backslash runs, joined directly; next line is raw text (its `=`/`:`/quotes/comments ordinary); dangling marker rejected.
- Inline comments only when a blank immediately precedes `;`/`#`, disabled inside quotes.
- Unicode-safe via UTF-16 code-unit scanning with substring copies (preserves surrogate pairs).
- `print` double-quotes every value and section name so `parse(print(doc)) == doc`.

- **`scanner.mbt`** (new) — line splitting (LF/CRLF, trailing-empty drop), whitespace/comment helpers, quote scanning, per-carrier escape decoding, inline-comment detection, continuation run counting, section parsing.

### Key behaviors implemented
- Global entries + named sections; repeated headers re-open; duplicate keys last-wins.
- First `=`/`:` wins; keys trimmed, non-empty, no control chars; escapes decoded in values only.
- Quoted values (`"..."`, `'...'`) closed on the same line, comment markers literal, only whitespace/comment after the close; per-carrier escapes exactly per the spec table.
- Backslash continuation decided on the **raw** line (odd run = marker, even = literals), joined directly, whitespace before the marker preserved; dangling marker is an error.
- Inline comments require a preceding whitespace separator (so `key=#ff0000` keeps its value).
- `print` emits every value double-quoted and round-trips `parse(print(doc)) == doc`, including the quickcheck generators.

### Validation run
- `moon fmt` — clean

- `moon test` — **28/28 passed** (12 public + 16 added), including 1000 randomized round-trips and the no-panic property test.

### Judgment calls on ambiguous spec points
- **Section headers are strict**: only whitespace may follow `]` (no trailing inline comment), matching the spec's grammar `line := ws* (comment | section | kv | empty) ws*`.
- **Inline comments are detected on the raw value** before trimming (so `key= ; comment` has an empty value).
- **Continuation is assembled before the separator search**, but this only differs for the unlikely input where the first physical line has a marker but no separator.

### How it works (key decisions)
- **Streaming:** `read` may return fewer bytes than requested, so `read_exactly` loops until a value is complete and raises at end of stream. It reads small values into an exact buffer and large payloads in 4 KiB chunks, so an oversized length prefix (e.g. `2^31-1`) fails fast instead of allocating gigabytes.
- **Varints:** one `read_varint64` primitive handles the ten-byte limit, non-minimal forms (`80 00` = 0), bits-beyond-64 dropped (`80×9 7F` = 2^63) and eleventh-byte overflow; 32-bit readers truncate to the low 32 bits, `int32`/`enum` use two's-complement, `sint*` use zigzag.
- **Fixed width:** assembled/decomposed little-endian with bit reinterpretation, so NaN payloads, infinities and `-0.0` round-trip exactly.
- **Keys/unknown:** `(field_number << 3) | wire_type`, rejecting field 0 and wire types 6/7; `read_unknown` skips varint/I64/LEN/I32 and whole nested groups with matching end tags.
- **Opaque types:** `BytesReader`/`LimitedReader` are `pub struct`s with `priv` fields, satisfying the `declare pub type` declarations while keeping their representation internal.
- **Errors:** bare `raise` effects with descriptive `fail(...)` messages; malformed input never panics.

## How it works
- **Splitting** peels components off in grammar order (fragment → query → scheme → authority/path), preserving the `None` vs `Some("")` distinction exactly; a `:` is a scheme separator only when the prefix matches `ALPHA *(ALPHA/DIGIT/+/-/.)` (first-match-wins).
- **Validation** checks each component against its own character set, rejects malformed `%XX`, non-numeric ports, raw forbidden characters (space, `<>`, `\`, `^`, backtick, `{}`, `|`, `"`, controls, non-ASCII), malformed IPv6/IPvFuture literals, invalid schemes, and ambiguous authorities (>1 `@`, or >1 `:` on a non-bracketed host). IPv6 is validated structurally (single `::`, ≤7 explicit groups, strict `ls32`/dec-octet IPv4, zone IDs).
- **Resolution** is the literal §5.2.2 pseudocode in strict mode (`http:g` stays `http:g`), with dot-segment removal implemented as the RFC's two-buffer algorithm, so all normal and abnormal §5.4 examples resolve correctly.
